{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMzvWZYBEmbDMak8MJQt","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-SumMean.md ===\n# FEATURE: Sum And Mean\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Report the exact sum and mean of the non-null values of integer and number columns. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-TypesNumeric.md, FEATURE-MinMax.md |\n| Provides    | profile field sum, profile field mean |\n| Consumes    | column type decision, null rule, trimmed values |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThe `sum` and `mean` fields of each profile row summarize numeric columns. They are computed with\nexact arithmetic so that no digit string overflows and no binary floating point error enters the\nresult. Rounding happens once, when the value is written (see `FEATURE-DecimalFormat.md`).\n\n## Trigger\n\nEvery profile run (`csvstat <file>` and `csvstat --column <name> <file>`) computes `sum` and `mean`\nfor every column whose inferred type is `integer` or `number`.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Package: `internal/profile` accumulates, `internal/decimal` holds exact values.\n- Only non-null values participate. Null values (empty, `NA`, `N/A`, `NULL` ignoring case, after\n  trimming) are skipped.\n- Each value is parsed exactly: an integer into `big.Int`, a number into `big.Rat` through\n  `Rat.SetString`. `float32` and `float64` are never used on the data path.\n- `sum` is the exact total of the non-null values.\n- `mean` is the exact total divided by the count of non-null values, held as a `big.Rat`.\n- An `integer` column writes `sum` as a plain integer (an arbitrary-precision digit string). Its\n  `mean` is written by the decimal formatter.\n- A `number` column writes `sum` and `mean` through the decimal formatter.\n- A column of type `text`, `date`, `boolean`, or `empty` leaves `sum` and `mean` blank.\n- Columns are independent: a numeric column's sum never depends on another column.\n\n## Reads\n\n- The trimmed, null-classified values of the column and its inferred type.\n\n## Writes\n\n- The `sum` and `mean` cells of the profile row on standard output. No files, no persistence.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC summean-integer-exact ===\nIntent: An integer column reports the exact integer sum and the two-decimal mean of its values.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, getcontext\nfrom fractions import Fraction\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\n\ndef fmt(fr):\n    getcontext().prec = 200\n    d = Decimal(fr.numerator) / Decimal(fr.denominator)\n    return str(d.quantize(Decimal(\"0.01\"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))\n\n\ndef run(text, *opts):\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n        p = os.path.join(d, \"data.csv\")\n        with open(p, \"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n            fh.write(text)\n        return cli_runner(*opts, p)\n\n\nvals = [4, -7, 12, 100, 3]\ntext = \"v\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(str(v) for v in vals) + \"\\n\"\ncode, out, err = run(text)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nrow = rows[1]\ntotal = sum(vals)\nassert row[1] == \"integer\"\nassert row[7] == str(total)\nassert row[8] == fmt(Fraction(total, len(vals)))\n=== END AC summean-integer-exact ===\n\n=== AC summean-integer-bigint ===\nIntent: Integer sums beyond 64 bits are computed with arbitrary precision and never overflow.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, getcontext\nfrom fractions import Fraction\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\n\ndef fmt(fr):\n    getcontext().prec = 200\n    d = Decimal(fr.numerator) / Decimal(fr.denominator)\n    return str(d.quantize(Decimal(\"0.01\"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))\n\n\ndef run(text, *opts):\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n        p = os.path.join(d, \"data.csv\")\n        with open(p, \"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n            fh.write(text)\n        return cli_runner(*opts, p)\n\n\nvals = [10**30 + 7, 10**30 + 9, -(10**29), 99999999999999999999]\ntext = \"v\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(str(v) for v in vals) + \"\\n\"\ncode, out, err = run(text)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrow = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1]\ntotal = sum(vals)\nassert row[7] == str(total)\nassert row[8] == fmt(Fraction(total, len(vals)))\n=== END AC summean-integer-bigint ===\n\n=== AC summean-number-exact-decimal ===\nIntent: Number sums and means come from exact decimal values and are rounded half away from zero once.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, getcontext\nfrom fractions import Fraction\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\n\ndef fmt(fr):\n    getcontext().prec = 200\n    d = Decimal(fr.numerator) / Decimal(fr.denominator)\n    return str(d.quantize(Decimal(\"0.01\"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))\n\n\ndef run(text, *opts):\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n        p = os.path.join(d, \"data.csv\")\n        with open(p, \"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n            fh.write(text)\n        return cli_runner(*opts, p)\n\n\ncases = [[\"2.675\"], [\"0.1\", \"0.2\", \"0.7\"], [\"-2.675\", \"1.005\", \"3\"], [\"1.0049\", \"1.0049\"]]\nfor vals in cases:\n    text = \"v\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(vals) + \"\\n\"\n    code, out, err = run(text)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    row = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))[1]\n    frs = [Fraction(v) for v in vals]\n    total = sum(frs)\n    assert row[1] == \"number\"\n    assert row[7] == fmt(total)\n    assert row[8] == fmt(total / len(frs))\n=== END AC summean-number-exact-decimal ===\n\n=== AC summean-nulls-skipped ===\nIntent: Null values are excluded from both the sum and the divisor of the mean.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; |\n| Description | Write numeric statistics with exactly two decimals, rounded half away from zero once from the exact value. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-SumMean.md, FEATURE-Median.md |\n| Provides    | decimal formatter for min, max, sum, mean, and median |\n| Consumes    | exact big.Rat values from sum, mean, median, min, max |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nNumeric statistics are written in one canonical shape. Rounding is performed exactly once, at\noutput, from the exact rational value, so that results are reproducible and independent of\nbinary floating point.\n\n## Trigger\n\nEvery profile row of an `integer` or `number` column writes its numeric cells through this\nformatter.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Package: `internal/decimal` exposes a function taking a `*big.Rat` and returning a string.\n- For a `number` column: `min`, `max`, `sum`, `mean`, and `median` are two-decimal strings.\n- For an `integer` column: `mean` and `median` are two-decimal strings; `min`, `max`, and `sum`\n  are plain integers with no decimal point.\n- Two-decimal form: scale the absolute value by 100, round half up on the absolute value\n  (ties move away from zero) using `big.Int` arithmetic, then insert the decimal point. There is\n  always at least one digit before the point and exactly two after it.\n- A leading `-` appears only when the rounded result is non-zero and the value is negative. A\n  negative value that rounds to zero is written without a sign.\n- No thousands separator, no exponent, no leading `+`.\n- Rounding is applied once to the exact value; an already rounded value is never rounded again.\n- Non-numeric column types are unaffected and keep their own rules.\n\n## Reads\n\n- Exact `big.Rat` values produced by the sum, mean, median, and min/max computations.\n\n##  return (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2]) / 2\n\n\ndef run(text, *opts):\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n        p = os.path.join(d, \"data.csv\")\n        with open(p, \"w\", newline=\"\") BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-SumMean.md ===\n# FEATURE: Sum And Mean\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Report the exact sum and mean of the non-null values of integer and number columns. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-TypesNumeric.md, FEATURE-MinMax.md |\n| Provides    | profile field sum, profile field mean |\n| Consumes    | column type decision, null rule, trimmed values |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThe `sum` and `mean` fields of each profile row summarize numeric columns. They are computed with\nexact arithmetic so that no digit string overflows and no binary floating point error enters the\nresult. Rounding happens once, when the value is written (see `FEATURE-DecimalFormat.md`).\n\n## Trigger\n\nEvery profile run (`csvstat <file>` and `csvstat --column <name> <file>`) computes `sum` and `mean`\nfor every column whose inferred type is `integer` or `number`.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Package: `internal/profile` accumulates, `internal/decimal` holds exact values.\n- Only non-null values participate. Null values (empty, `NA`, `N/A`, `NULL` ignoring case, after\n  trimming) are skipped.\n- Each value is parsed exactly: an integer into `big.Int`, a number into `big.Rat` through\n  `Rat.SetString`. `float32` and `float64` are never used on the data path.\n- `sum` is the exact total of the non-null values.\n- `mean` is the exact total divided by the count of non-null values, held as a `big.Rat`.\n- An `integer` column writes `sum` as a plain integer (an arbitrary-precision digit string). Its\n  `mean` is written by the decimal formatter.\n- A `number` column writes `sum` and `mean` through the decimal formatter.\n- A column of type `text`, `date`, `boolean`, or `empty` leaves `sum` and `mean` blank.\n- Columns are independent: a numeric column's sum never depends on another column.\n\n## Reads\n\n- The trimmed, null-classified values of the column and its inferred type.\n\n## Writes\n\n- The `sum` and `mean` cells of the profile row on standard output. No files, no persistence.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC summean-integer-exact ===\nIntent: An integer column reports the exact integer sum and the two-decimal mean of its values.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; |\n| Description | Write numeric statistics with exactly two decimals, rounded half away from zero once from the exact value. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-SumMean.md, FEATURE-Median.md |\n| Provides    | decimal formatter for min, max, sum, mean, and median |\n| Consumes    | exact big.Rat values from sum, mean, median, min, max |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nNumeric statistics are There is\n  always at least one digit before the point and exactly two after it.\n- A leading `-` appears only when the rounded result is non-zero and the value is negative. never rounded again.\n- Non-numeric column types are unaffected and keep their own rules.\n\n## Reads\n\n- Exact `big.Rat` values produced by the sum, mean, median, and min/max computations.\n\n## decimalformat-fixture-files ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Rounding is performed exactly once, from the exact `big.Rat`, never from a rounded intermediate.\n- No `float32` FEATURE-DecimalFormat.md |\n| Provides    | csvstat --column <name> <file> |\n| Consumes    | csvstat <file> profile rows, trimmed header names |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nLets a user profile a single column of a wide file without reading every row of the full profile.\n\n## Trigger\n\n`csvstat --column <name> <file>`. `--column` cannot be combined with `--freq` (a usage error owned\nby `FEATURE-UsageErrors.md`).\n\n## Behavior\n\n- The output is the profile header `column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median`\n  followed by exactly one row, the row of the named column, identical in every field to the row the\n  full profile writes for that column.\n- The `<name>` argument matches a trimmed header name exactly and case-sensitively. Header names\n  are trimmed of leading and trailing spaces before matching, so a file header ` Name ` is\n  selected by `Name`.\n- The statistics of the other columns are not written; the named column's values are still\n  validated like any other (a ragged record still rejects the file).\n- A name that is not in the header is rejected with exit 3 (owned by `FEATURE-ColumnAbsent.md`).\n- Output is CSV with `\\n` line endings produced by `encoding/csv`'s writer, so a field containing a\n  comma, quote, or newline is quoted.\n- Success exits 0.\n\n## Reads\n\n- The CSV file given on the command line.\n\n## Writes\n\n- Standard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC colselect-matches-full-profile-row ===\nIntent: For every column of the supplied files, --column writes the profile header and exactly the row the full profile writes for that column.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\nfor path in (\"sources/employees.csv\", \"sources/sensors.csv\", \"sources/orders.csv\", \"sources/header_only.csv\"):\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(path)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    full = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    header = full[0]\n    assert len(full) > 1\n    for row in full[1:]:\n        name = row[0]\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"--column\", name, path)\n        print(out)\n        print(err)\n        assert code == 0\n        picked = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n        assert len(picked) == 2\n        assert picked[0] == header\n        assert picked[1] == row\n=== END AC colselect-matches-full-profile-row ===\n\n=== AC colselect-only-named-column ===\nIntent: The output of --column contains one data row whose first cell is the name supplied, even for the last column of the file.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport os\nimport tempfile\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\n\ndef run(text, *opts):\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:\n        p = os.path.join(d, \"data.csv\")\n        with open(p, \"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n            fh.write(text)\n        return cli_runner(*opts, p)\n\n\nnames = [\"alpha\", \"beta\", \"gamma\", \"delta\"]\ntext = \",\".join(names) + \"\\n1,x,true,2025-01-02\\n2,y,false,2025-02-03\\n\"\nfor name in names:\n    code, out, err = run(text, \"--column\", name)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    assert len(rows) == 2\n    assert rows[1][0] == name\n=== END AC colselect-only-named-column ===\n\n=== AC colselect-trimmed-header-and-values ===\nIntent: A padded header is selected by its trimmed name and the padded values are trimmed before they are profiled.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\n\nfrom drydock_go import cli_runner\n\npath = \"sources/header_only.csv\"\nwith open(path, newline=\"\") as fh:\n    name = next(csv.reader(fh))[1].strip()\ncode, out, err = cli_runner(\"--column\", name, path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert len(rows) == 2\nassert rows[1][0] == name\nassert rows[1][1] == \"empty\"\nassert rows[1][2] == str(0)\n=== END AC colselect-header-only-file ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- `--column` never writes more than one data row.\n- Column names are not matched case-insensitively and are not fuzzy matched.\n- Application code never reads `sources/run.sh` or any supplied data file and never embeds an answer.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ColumnAbsent.md ===\n# FEATURE: Column Absent\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261025 V1 |\n| Description | Reject a --column or --freq name that is not in the header with exit code 3 and nothing on standard output. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-ColumnSelect.md, FEATURE-RejectMalformed.md |\n| Provides    | exit 3 for an absent column name |\n| Consumes    | csvstat --column <name> <file>, csvstat --freq <name> <file>, rejection exit mapping |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nA misspelled or absent column name is a rejected request, not an empty result. The caller must be\nable to tell it apart from a usage error (exit 2) and from an unreadable file (exit 1).\n\n## Trigger\n\n`csvstat --column <name> <file>` or `csvstat --freq <name> [--top <n>] <file>` where `<name>`\nmatches no trimmed header name of the file.\n\n## Behavior\n\n- Matching is exact and case-sensitive against trimmed header names (`salary` does not select\n  `Salary`).\n- The check happens after the file is read and validated and before any output is written, so\n  standard output stays empty.\n- The process exits 3 and writes one diagnostic line to standard error naming the file.\n- A name that is present is unaffected and continues to succeed.\n- A file that cannot be read still exits 1 first, and a usage error still exits 2 first; this\n  story only owns the absent-name rejection.\n- A file that is itself rejected (empty, ragged, bad header) exits 3 for that reason, with the same\n  empty standard output.\n\n## Reads\n\n- The CSV file header after trimming.\n\n## Writes\n\n- One diagnostic line on standard error. Nothing on standard output.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC colabsent-column-exit-3 ===\nIntent: --column with a name absent from the header exits 3 and writes nothing to standard output.\nSuite: scoped\nRequires: executable=go;
